title: Arts participation is a socially patterned cultural resource associated with connection
source_unit: National Endowment for the Arts analysis of Census Household Pulse Survey Phase 4.1 cycles 04-07

observations.period: April 2 through July 22, 2024; four Household Pulse cycles

denominator.unit: U.S. adults in the Household Pulse Survey estimates

in_person_arts_attendance.unit: percent attending a live performance and/or art exhibit in the previous month

arts_creation.unit: percent creating, practicing, or performing art in the previous month

arts_access_agreement.unit: percent agreeing there were plenty of neighborhood or community arts opportunities

low_income_attendance.unit: percent of adults earning under $25,000 attending an arts event in the previous month

high_income_attendance.unit: percent of adults earning $200,000 or more attending an arts event in the previous month

arts_attendance_support_association.value: arts attendees reported always/usually receiving needed social and emotional support at 29.8%/39.5%, versus 23.4%/24.1% among non-attendees

observations.method: NEA descriptive analysis of four Census Household Pulse Survey Phase 4.1 cycles; attendance, creation, access, loneliness, social/emotional support, and social-contact measures are retained as separate survey surfaces.
observations.uncertainty: The source is repeated cross-sectional and correlational. It does not establish whether arts participation caused support or whether prior resources and social ties enabled both. The previous-month window does not measure durable participation, quality, meaning, organizational continuity, or later civic action.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adults with comparisons by age, gender, race/ethnicity, education, household income, and arts attendance or creation status.
observations.counterinterpretation: Arts attendance may be a marker of money, time, health, transportation, education, place, prior social ties, or selection into participation rather than an independent cause of connection. A person can have meaningful cultural participation outside the surveyed activities.

related_sources.claim: NEA identifies the brief as part of its arts-participation research and Census-administered data program.
Census Household Pulse Survey provides the underlying timely social and economic survey context.

boundary: This record adds a cultural-infrastructure association: arts access and participation are distributed unevenly and correlate with reported social connection. It does not establish an arts treatment effect, durable belonging, community repair, organizational success, or political action.
